description: We are ASTRAVERA, a passionate team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to explore innovative ways to use NASA data and space technology to support sustainable agriculture. We believe in creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving. We welcome enthusiastic members with skills in coding, research, data analysis, design, and innovative thinking. Together, let's turn ideas into impactful solutions!
summary: Our project, ASTRAVERA, aims to help farmers make smarter decisions using NASA satellite data and space technology. We propose developing a smart agricultural support system that uses information about rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, and weather patterns to identify possible risks to crops. It will help farmers understand changing environmental conditions, plan irrigation, and adapt farming methods to climate changes. By turning NASA data into useful agricultural insights, our idea aims to reduce crop losses, improve water management, and support sustainable farming. This project connects space science with agriculture to create a better and more resilient future for farmers.
details: ASTRAVERA is a proposed smart agriculture project that connects NASA satellite data with farming to support better agricultural decisions. Our idea is to analyse rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, and vegetation conditions using NASA Earth observation data. The system aims to identify possible drought conditions, water stress, and crop-related risks. It will help farmers understand environmental changes and make informed decisions about irrigation and crop management. We plan to explore NASA POWER, SMAP, and MODIS/VIIRS datasets to develop a user-friendly agricultural support platform. The creative aspect of our project is combining space technology with real-world farming needs. Our goal is to promote sustainable agriculture, improve water management, reduce potential crop losses, and support farmers in adapting to climate change. At this stage, we have prepared the project concept and presentation. The software prototype is yet to be developed.
